deliveryNotes: The question-type menu represents format information, not an exercise/test.
The title What skills are tested? is educational; it is not a proficiency score.
Listening applies to both IELTS Academic and General Training; this Reading list is specifically Academic Reading.
Only show content supported by the mapped source rows and the linked official format pages.

questionTypes.title: Multiple choice
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: In Multiple choice questions, you are given a question followed by three possible options (A, B, or C), or a sentence beginning with three possible endings. Sometimes you are given a longer list of options and must choose two or more correct answers (e.g. choose two letters from A–E). Questions follow the chronological order of the audio recording.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests a broad range of listening skills: understanding the central idea, identifying detailed factual information, following a sequence of events, and distinguishing between primary facts and subtle distractors.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Read the instructions carefully to verify whether one or multiple letters are required. Distractors will mention words from the wrong options to test your comprehension.

questionTypes.title: Matching
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: In Matching questions, you are asked to connect a numbered list of items heard in the listening text to a set of options (usually categorized letters, such as types of facilities, responsibilities, or hotel ratings).
questionTypes.skillsTested: Assesses your ability to listen for specific information, trace connections between items and categories, and recognize paraphrase and synonyms used in natural speech.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Focus on the relationship and meaning rather than listening for exact words, as the recording will use synonyms for the options.

questionTypes.title: Plan/map/diagram labelling
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are provided with a visual plan (e.g. a building layout or floor plan), a map of an outdoor area (e.g. a town or campsite), or a diagram of a piece of equipment, and must complete the labels. You may be asked to choose answers from a box of options or write words from the audio.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Evaluates your ability to understand spatial descriptions, directional language (e.g. 'north-east', 'to your left', 'adjacent to', 'opposite'), and follow a speaker navigating through an environment.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Orient yourself with the visual layout before the recording begins: identify starting points, landmarks, compass directions, and existing labels.

questionTypes.title: Form/note/table/flow-chart completion
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You must complete gaps in an outline summarizing part or all of the audio recording. The outline may be an administrative form (e.g. customer name, telephone number, address), a set of structured notes (headings and bullet points), a data table (categorizing information into rows and columns), or a flow-chart illustrating sequential stages in a process.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests your ability to identify key facts, record specific numerical and personal details, recognize classifications, and trace procedural stages.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Pay strict attention to the word limit (e.g. 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER'). Words taken directly from the audio must be spelled correctly.

questionTypes.title: Sentence completion
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given a set of sentences that summarize core information from the listening text, each containing one or more gaps that you must fill using words heard in the audio.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Assesses your ability to identify essential factual points, recognize relationships such as cause-and-effect or conditional sequences, and understand how spoken ideas map to written sentences.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: The completed sentence must be grammatically accurate and must not exceed the stated word limit. Numbers may be written as figures or words.

questionTypes.title: Short-answer questions
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are presented with direct factual questions and must write a short answer using information heard in the recording. Some questions may ask you to list two or three specific points.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests your capability to locate and extract concrete factual information (e.g. prices, times, dates, locations, quantities, materials).
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Keep answers concise. Do not write full sentences where one or two words are sufficient. Ensure spelling is accurate.

questionTypes.title: Multiple choice
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You must choose the best answer from four options (A, B, C, or D), or complete a sentence stem by choosing from four options. Occasionally, you must choose multiple correct answers from a longer list (e.g. two from five).
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests detailed understanding of specific information, recognition of main ideas, and discernment between closely related arguments.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Questions follow the order of information in the passage. Eliminate options that contain partial truths or extreme words not supported by the text.

questionTypes.title: Identifying information (True/False/Not Given)
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given a series of factual statements and must decide whether each statement agrees with the information in the text (TRUE), contradicts the text (FALSE), or if there is no information on it in the text (NOT GIVEN).
questionTypes.skillsTested: Assesses ability to identify specific factual information, understand exact nuances, and crucially distinguish between facts that are contradicted and facts that are simply not mentioned.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: 'False' means the passage directly contradicts the statement. 'Not Given' means the passage neither confirms nor contradicts it. Base answers solely on the text, not personal knowledge.

questionTypes.title: Identifying writer views (Yes/No/Not Given)
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given statements and must decide whether they reflect the views or claims of the author: YES (agrees with the writer's claim), NO (contradicts the writer's claim), or NOT GIVEN (it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this).
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests recognition of an author's stated opinions, hypotheses, attitudes, and subjective reasoning, as opposed to purely objective facts.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Notice the difference: True/False assesses objective facts; Yes/No assesses the author's viewpoint and arguments.

questionTypes.title: Matching information
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given a list of statements containing specific information (e.g. an example, a reason, a summary, an explanation, or a historical background) and must identify the letter of the paragraph in the passage where it is found.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Assesses scanning skills and the ability to locate specific information, examples, definitions, and arguments across multiple paragraphs.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Paragraphs may be used more than once if instructions state 'NB: You may use any letter more than once'. Information statements do not follow text order.

questionTypes.title: Matching headings
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given a list of headings (indicated by Roman numerals i, ii, iii, etc.) and must match each heading to the correct paragraph or section of the reading passage. There will always be more headings than paragraphs.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Evaluates understanding of paragraph-level main ideas and themes, distinguishing the central message from supporting details.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Read the entire paragraph to grasp its core purpose rather than relying only on the first sentence, which can sometimes be an introductory hook or transition.

questionTypes.title: Matching features
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given a list of statements and must match them to a group of features from the text (such as names of scientists, researchers, inventions, organizations, or historical periods).
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests scanning for named entities and synthesizing what each person or group said, discovered, or argued across different parts of the text.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Options may be used more than once if permitted. Scan the passage first to mark all occurrences of the names before reading the statements.

questionTypes.title: Matching sentence endings
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given the first half of a sentence based on the passage and must choose the correct ending from a list of options (A, B, C, etc.). There are always more endings than sentence beginnings.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests comprehension of complex sentence logic, cause-and-effect relationships, and synthesis of ideas across a sentence.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Questions follow the order of the passage. Ensure your selected ending is both grammatically compatible and supported by the text.

questionTypes.title: Sentence completion
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You must complete sentences by filling in gaps with words taken directly from the reading passage, observing the stated word limit.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Assesses ability to locate specific information and choose appropriate lexical items that fit syntactically into the sentence.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Do not change the form of words taken from the text (e.g. do not change a noun to an adjective). Hyphenated words count as single words.

questionTypes.title: Summary/note/table/flow-chart completion
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are given a summary of part or all of the passage (which may be a connected paragraph, a set of notes, a structured table, or a flow-chart) and must complete the missing words, either from the passage or from a box of provided options.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests ability to understand a condensed overview, identify paraphrases, and select vocabulary that maintains grammatical correctness.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: If choosing from a box of options, the options will often be synonyms of the words appearing in the passage rather than identical words.

questionTypes.title: Diagram label completion
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You must label a technical diagram or illustration (e.g. an engineering device, an architectural blueprint, or a natural process) using words from the passage.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Assesses ability to connect detailed spatial and procedural written descriptions with visual representations.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Follow the numbers on the diagram sequentially and ensure your answers respect the word limit.

questionTypes.title: Short-answer questions
questionTypes.whatIsInvolved: You are asked direct questions about the passage and must answer using words or numbers taken directly from the text within a strict word count.
questionTypes.skillsTested: Tests ability to locate and retrieve specific factual details quickly and accurately.
questionTypes.questionCount: Variable: there is no fixed number assigned to this type.
questionTypes.practicalNote: Do not write complete sentences. Write only the precise words needed to answer the question, and adhere strictly to the word limit.
